clue.text: Put out, replacing ex, daughter lives like a VIP

indicators.note: one thing replacing another means a swap inside the word: some letters leave and others take their place

parts.note: a fire that is put out has been doused
these two letters are taken literally, and are the ones thrown out
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
'lives' as in exists, which is IS

explanation.surface: A former partner gets turfed out and the daughter moves in, living it up like a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ex' looks like a former partner, but it is just the two letters that go; the daughter and 'lives' take their place at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A VIP is someone eminent and respected, and an eminent, respected person is called distinguished.

clue.text: Cooked real soup and pud, serving two functions

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or mixed up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; pud is British slang for pudding

explanation.surface: A dish of soup and pudding together covers two courses at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dual-purpose has two uses, so it carries out two different functions.

clue.text: Total bill for tree

parts.note: the total is the sum
AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill

explanation.surface: The full invoice for felling a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumac is a small shrubby tree whose dried berries give a tart Middle Eastern spice.

clue.text: Price not right, unfortunately, for such farm produce

indicators.note: things that turn out unfortunately have gone wrong, so the letters fall out of order

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A farmer grumbles that the crops are not fetching the right price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' is part of the anagram, not a sign that a letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: An intercrop is a secondary crop grown in the rows between a main crop, so it is a harvest from the farm.

clue.text: Astronomer's sound proof connected with constellation

indicators.note: connected pieces are joined end to end
sound tells us to hear the next word spoken rather than read it

parts.note: a galley proof is a printer's first proof of type
Leo, the Lion, is a constellation of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A stargazer has evidence, backed up by a particular group of stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound proof' reads as soundproof; here sound signals a homophone, and the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Galileo Galilei was the Italian scientist who first turned a telescope on the night sky.

clue.text: Superior blood I brought from Germany to men

indicators.note: one piece brought to another is set right next to it

parts.note: ich is German for I
OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A German aristocrat claims his blue blood has passed down to the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Superior' means belonging to the gods on high, not just better.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth ichor is the ethereal fluid that runs in the veins of the gods instead of blood.

clue.text: Food mother knocked over cutting her minced beef roll

indicators.note: to cut into a word is to break it apart and sit inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something knocked over ends up the other way round, and in a down entry it is turned upwards

parts.note: grub is slang for food
an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Mum's cooking is upset when she is interrupted making a meat roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minced' looks like an instruction to scramble her, but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamburger is a patty of ground beef served in a bread bun, a roll.

clue.text: Flower of French and English (and Welsh and Scots!)

parts.note: de is French for of
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A bloom that belongs to France, England, Wales and Scotland too.
explanation.walkthrough: A flower here is something that flows, a river. One River Dee runs through Wales and England, another through Scotland, which the bracket celebrates.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosswords use flower to mean a river, since a river is a thing that flows.

clue.text: Oil producer's friend to west of motorway

indicators.note: in an across entry west is the left, so the first piece goes before the second

parts.note: an informal word for a friend
British motorways are numbered M1, M25 and so on

explanation.surface: An oil company boss's friend lives somewhere just west of the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The oil palm's fruit is pressed to make palm oil, so the tree itself is an oil producer.

clue.text: Metal trim fixed with head of heavy forging tool

indicators.note: something fixed has been rigged or tampered with, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of heavy

explanation.surface: A metalworker fits metal trim using a heavy tool from the forge.
explanation.definitionFit: A tilt hammer is a large pivoted power hammer once used in forges to beat out iron.

clue.text: Spooky police officer, not at home, misses old gangster

indicators.note: 'not at home' says the word for home is to be absent from what came before
whatever the word misses is left out of it

parts.note: a police rank
being in means being at home
O is the abbreviation for old
Al Capone, the Chicago gangster of the 1920s

explanation.surface: A creepy detective, never at home, misses a notorious crook from the past.
explanation.walkthrough: INSPECTOR loses IN and then its O, leaving SPECTR, and the gangster AL is added: SPECTRAL. 'Old gangster' tempts as one phrase, but 'old' is the O dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectral describes something ghostly, like a spectre, which is exactly what spooky means.

clue.text: Time to avoid disturbance, being ready in Belarus

indicators.note: the time letter is to avoid the word, so it is kept out of it

parts.note: trouble is unrest or disturbance
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone in Minsk is keen to slip away before any unrest breaks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is old slang for cash (from 'ready money'), so ready in Belarus is its currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The Belarusian currency is the rouble, so the cash a Belarusian carries is counted in roubles.

clue.text: Member's delayed outside old city parliament

parts.note: a leg is a limb or member, and 's is 'is'

indicators.note: being outside something means wrapped around it

parts.note: something delayed arrives late
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: An MP turns up late outside the historic city's parliament building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests an MP, but here it is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: A legislature is the law-making assembly of a state, and a parliament is one such body.

clue.text: Hairy goody-goody guarding military transport

indicators.note: a guard stands around what it protects, so one word surrounds the rest

parts.note: a goody-goody makes a show of being virtuous
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a car is a means of transport

explanation.surface: A hirsute prig escorts an army convoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hairy' looks like a description of the goody-goody, but it is the slang definition: risky.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a hairy situation is a dangerous, nerve-racking one, which is what precarious means.

clue.text: Cooked food, as served at first in part of church?

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the next word

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
taken as written

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter only

parts.note: the opening letter of served
a part in a play is a role

explanation.surface: A hot meal dished up at the start of a church event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of church' is read backwards as the church's part, so the part follows the church, and the insertion goes into the church abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A casserole is a dish of meat and vegetables slowly baked in a lidded pot.

clue.text: A question a king notes that may or may not be raised about convulsions in the main

indicators.text: that may or may not be raised
indicators.note: in a down entry raised means read upwards, and 'may or may not' says one pair is turned and the other left alone
about means going round, so these letters are placed on either side

parts.note: E and S are musical notes, taken twice
taken as written
QU is the abbreviation for question
taken as written
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Someone asks a monarch about seizures, with notes that might or might not be brought up.
explanation.walkthrough: Two pairs of notes go round the rest: one pair is turned upwards and the other is not, which is what 'may or may not' means. 'The main' is the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaquake is an earthquake under the sea floor, a violent shaking of the ocean, the main in old poetic usage.

clue.text: Musical engagement preceding current movie

indicators.note: one thing preceding another comes first, fixing the order of the two pieces

parts.note: a gig is a booking for a band to play
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A band plays a set just before a new film is screened.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigi is the 1958 Hollywood musical film that won the Oscar for best picture.

clue.text: Cold-blooded creatures show off no end

indicators.note: with no end, the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: to show off is to brag

explanation.surface: Reptiles endlessly flaunt themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Boas are snakes, and snakes, like all reptiles, are cold-blooded animals.

clue.text: In Russian city, American poet describing a polar feature

parts.note: Perm is a city in the Urals
taken as written
Robert Frost, the New England poet

explanation.surface: A visiting American poet in Russia writes about the Arctic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Russian city' sets the scene; Perm comes first, then A, then the poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Permafrost is ground frozen all year round, a characteristic of the Arctic and Antarctic regions.

clue.text: Cut back on rubbish?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to reduce gradually, as a firm reduces its stock or staff
second meaning: to criticise or disparage, used as a verb

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish' looks like a noun, as in cutting back on waste, but it is the verb meaning to knock something.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to reduce something steadily and to criticise it unkindly.

clue.text: Deprived female wearing round felt cap

indicators.note: whatever is wearing a hat is inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a beret is a flat round cap, usually of felt
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A poor woman goes about in a shabby felt hat.
explanation.walkthrough: F goes inside BERET, after its fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bereft has had something taken away from them, which is to be deprived of it.

clue.text: Bloomer made by union leader taking pound in gratuity

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the next word

parts.note: a tip is a gratuity

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of union
L, from Latin libra, is the symbol for a pound

explanation.surface: A trade union boss blunders by pocketing a pound as a tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' joins union's leader to the pound; both then go in the tip. A bloomer is also a blunder, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a crossword name for a flower, something that blooms, and a tulip is a spring flower.

clue.text: Mischievous-sounding visit mostly concerning ratings, etc?

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word but not all, so its last letter goes
-sounding tells us to use what the word sounds like, not how it is spelt

parts.note: naughty is a word for mischievous
to pay a call is to visit

explanation.surface: A cheeky social call to discuss audience ratings.
explanation.walkthrough: Ratings are ordinary sailors in the navy, not viewing figures; the question mark warns that the definition is cryptic.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical means to do with ships and seamen, and naval ratings are the seamen below officer rank.

clue.text: Partially pithecoid, a horrible state

indicators.note: partially says only part of the following words is used, a run of their letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of pithecoid, the word a and the start of horrible

explanation.surface: Being part ape-like is a dreadful condition to be in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like condition, but it is a US state; pithecoid means ape-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is a state in the north-western United States.

clue.text: A lot of fish to transfer finally into pan is child's responsibility

parts.note: a school is a large group of fish swimming together

indicators.note: one thing going into another is placed inside it

parts.note: a wok is a Chinese frying pan

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of transfer

explanation.surface: Tipping the fish into the frying pan is a job for the kids.
explanation.definitionFit: Lessons and homework set at school are a pupil's own duty to get done.

clue.text: Cut-price salad ingredient

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the last letter of the word is lopped off

parts.note: the price of something is its cost

explanation.surface: A cheap item for the salad bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut-price' reads as discounted, but the hyphen hides an instruction to shorten.
explanation.definitionFit: Cos is a variety of lettuce with long crisp leaves, the romaine used in Caesar salad.

clue.text: Spirit associated with a Mediterranean plant

indicators.note: things associated with each other are placed together, side by side

parts.note: taken as written
rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.surface: A liqueur flavoured with a southern European herb.
explanation.walkthrough: The spirit is named first but placed second, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Arums are a genus of lily-like plants native to Europe and the lands around the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Way Essex town's character is an aid to progress?

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
Epping is a market town in Essex, England
the tone of a place is its character

explanation.surface: The character of a road in an Essex town helps it get ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s of the town joins on to the character, so the word break moves when the pieces are run together.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepping stone is literally a stone to cross water on, and figuratively a stage that helps someone advance.
